exercise.name: Standing hip abduction (chair support)

class_text.good: trunk upright, straight leg lifted sideways and lowered with control - at any range (the range is checked against the physio's target angle, not by the model)
class_text.knee: the knee of the lifted leg bends during the lift
class_text.leanin: the trunk tilts sideways toward the lifted leg
class_text.leanout: the trunk tilts sideways away from the lifted leg (toward the chair side)
class_text.shallow: the leg is lifted only a little (range too small) - merged into good for the model

exercise.note: 4 form classes: 'shallow' (small lift) was merged into good for the model - the range is the range rule below, against a target the physiotherapist sets per patient

model.name: e4 head on the frozen InceptionTime encoder of the final joint network
model.onnx_inputs: x: float32 (reps, C_sel, T_LEN) raw stored channels in e4_head.json heads.e4.input_selection order; f: float32 (reps, F) raw per-rep measures in heads.e4.features order, NaN allowed. Output 'probs': (reps, K) in heads.e4.classes order. Normalisation is inside the file.

mediapipe.api: MediaPipe Tasks PoseLandmarker (the same model and settings as e1-e3)
mediapipe.running_mode: VIDEO (recorded) or LIVE_STREAM (camera); timestamps in ms must increase
mediapipe.landmarks: normalized landmarks (x, y in 0..1 of the frame, z, visibility, presence) AND world landmarks (metres); keep the frame width/height: pixel = normalized x width / y height
mediapipe.camera: from the FRONT, the WHOLE body in view including both feet (unlike e1-e3: the ankles are the main points), phone upright at hip height about 2-3 m away; the chair beside the standing leg, the patient holding it; image NOT mirrored (un-mirror the selfie preview before MediaPipe), upright (rotate by the sensor orientation)

pipeline.module: reference_python/leg_ds.py: analyze_video(d, side=<lifted leg>, n_geo=0, rr_levels=())
pipeline.count_signal_text: leg angle away from the body (hip -> ankle line against the trunk's own axis, degrees)
pipeline.side: the LIFTED leg (the app asks it, or the physiotherapist sets it in the prescription); the patient stands on the other leg holding the chair. If the other leg clearly moves more, analyze_video uses it and reports side_conflict = true: show messages.side_conflict
pipeline.get_ready: ask the patient to stand still about 2 s before the first lift (the first-break reference)
pipeline.same_as_e1_e3: resampling to 30 Hz, rep segmentation (segment_reps), first-break baseline (baseline_frames), rep window (rep_window: start - 0.5 s .. end + 0.5 s), resampling to 64 frames (to_T): the same functions as e1-e3 (shoulder_lib / shoulder_ds)

e4.knee: Keep your {leg} knee straight while you lift the leg
e4.leanin: Keep your trunk upright - do not lean toward the leg you lift
e4.leanout: Keep your trunk upright - do not lean away from the leg (toward the chair)

messages.range_low: Good form - lift your leg a bit higher: target {target:.0f} deg, you reached {reached:.0f} deg
messages.unsure: Not sure about this rep - check that your whole body, feet included, is in view
messages.partial: Rep cut by the start/end of the recording - not scored
messages.side_conflict: It looks like you are lifting your other leg - check the side chosen for this exercise

feedback.rule: confidence < min_confidence -> 'unsure'; label != good -> the class message; label == good -> range check (below the target -> range_low, else good). Partial reps (cut by the start/end) are counted, not scored.

range.measure_text: leg angle away from the body at the top of the rep (degrees); it is per-rep measure g4_abd_leg_peak of analyze_video (also in f)
range.order: 1) the physiotherapist's target angle for the patient (stored with the prescription); 2) else relative_fraction x the patient's usual lift (median peak of their good reps, e.g. of the first session); 3) else fixed_threshold_deg
range.why: range of motion is person-specific (full lift ~31-60 deg between people): leave-one-person-out, a target relative to the person's own lift was right for 95.4% of the reps vs 85.7% for one fixed angle. Judged only on good-form reps: leaning changes the leg angle (it is measured against the trunk).
